body:
The three documents agree on more than they contest, and it is worth fixing that before deciding anything: the withdrawal from conversation is the most distinctive feature of the situation; the living-arrangement question is the agreed terminus if engagement keeps failing (the account's step 5 and the rival's r11 converge on this independently, and convergence under different framings is the strongest joint signal on offer); and the supplied material is genuinely thin — thin as a fact about what was provided, not merely as the account's characterization, since we do not know the chores, the history, or whether the withdrawing friend has said anything.

On that last point I part from the objection's framing while keeping its conclusion. The objection says "thin" is the author's characterization rather than a feature of the situation; that overstates. But the conclusion — thin material licenses tentative probes rather than a confident sequence — survives the correction, and I would add what none of the three documents quite says: thinness here marks a division of labor, not only a caution. The person asking was present for the disputes and has access to their content; this inquiry does not. So the right deliverable is discriminators the asker can apply to material we cannot see, not a verdict reached on material that is thin. A well-designed first move is precisely one that generates the missing material.

What I take up from the objection is its central demand: the ambiguity reading should sit as one rival among three, not as the working hypothesis with caveats appended. The three readings — ambiguity about what the words specified, renegotiation about whether the terms still bind after a schedule change, legitimacy about who has standing to enforce — are distinguishable, and they are distinguishable in the content of the disputes. "You said bins by Thursday" answered by "my shift changed" is the renegotiation signature. "Who made you the scorekeeper" is the legitimacy signature. Genuinely being unable to say what was agreed is the ambiguity signature. I also take up the objection's attack on the recurrence test and strengthen it: the test is weak in both directions. Falling recurrence is compatible with every reading — a tighter spec on a lopsided arrangement is still lopsided, as the objection says — and continuing recurrence is compatible with a refused or contested spec, so it does not cleanly refute ambiguity either. The test gains power only with two additions the objection names and one it does not: watch for symptom migration (friction reappearing as new complaint items), watch for re-onset after the next schedule change, and combine with the rival's diagnostic below.

What I take up from the rival is, first, the single best addition across both critiques: whether the withdrawing flatmate engages with the content of a proposal or pulls back from the proposal's form. That observation converts the account's first move from a committed remedy into a test, and it directly repairs the weakness the objection found. Second, the truce-shaped arrangements — owned zones, rotations with default outcomes nobody has to negotiate in the moment. The rival undersells these: they are robust across readings, because they shrink the specification surface (less to be ambiguous about) and mutual exposure (less to feel coerced by) at the same time. Their costs are real: some efficiency, and — sharper — coverage. Bins and shared shopping, the account's own recurring examples, cannot be zoned; a truce with no default rule for the unzonables fails on exactly the hardest cases. What I revise in the rival is its opener. Asking a withdrawn person "what do you think the flat is — a unit or three private lives?" is the big-meaning question in one-on-one dress, and it risks the conversion the account warned against: task dispute into identity dispute. The unit-versus-privacy question is better asked in practical clothing, as a menu option the friend can pick without defending a philosophy.

What survives from the account: the small one-on-one ask as the vehicle; the prohibition on moral language and live scorekeeping, which both critiques leave untouched; and the three-column spec itself, which survives with a new rationale the account did not claim — its third column, what happens when someone cannot do it, is already a renegotiation accommodation, so the format quietly builds for one of the rival hypotheses. What gets revised is the frame: not steps toward a settlement but one small probe with explicit branches.

The probe I would run. One low-pressure conversation with the withdrawing flatmate, separate and kept separate, offering a genuine menu with no penalty for either choice: (a) pick two or three recurring things and draft what counts as done, by when, and what happens if a shift blows it up; or (b) each person owns a zone, nobody audits anybody, with one agreed default rule for what cannot be zoned. Then let the reaction do the diagnostic work. Content-engagement with (a) supports the ambiguity reading: tighten the items and watch recurrence, migration, and re-onset — with a standing commitment that falling recurrence accompanied by migrating complaints counts against the ambiguity reading, not as success with more specs to write. Preference for (b), or pullback from anything written at all, supports the unit-versus-privacy reading: build the truce properly, unzonables included, and check the design against the free-rider horn, since zones and defaults can quietly shift load. Refusal of both, or disputes about standing rather than content, is the legitimacy or relational signature: stop iterating formats and name the living-arrangement question directly. One scoping commitment, drawn from the account's spirit and the rival's r10: offer each format at most once or twice; re-proposing formats repeatedly is how the asker becomes the thing being avoided. Note also what the menu does to the framing dispute between the account and the objection: it does not settle which has the better prior reading, it puts both remedies on the table and lets the friend's reaction, rather than our plausibility ranking, select — and if the objection's own caveat is right that ambiguity was the plainest reading all along, the probe still works; option (a) simply gets chosen.

What remains open is most of what matters: which reading is right; whether the withdrawing friend is acting in good faith, which every input correctly declines to judge; and one thing none of the three inputs asked — who the asker is inside the dispute structure. The probe's reception may depend heavily on whether the person offering the menu is already heard as the scorekeeper; if so, the legitimacy reading is live from the start, and having the other, less-implicated flatmate make the offer is worth considering. The material is silent on all of this, and the probe, unlike another round of framing, is designed to settle some of it.

Treat the reaction as the diagnostic in c5.","action":"A single one-on-one menu offer, kept separate, not staged as a prelude to a household-wide settlement.","consequence":"The friend's reaction, rather than a prior plausibility ranking among framings, selects the branch; both the account's and the objection's preferred remedies are on the table as options.","depends":["c5"],"mentions":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c3","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r6","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r8","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r10"]},{"id":"u2","type":"use","text":"Branch rules: content-engagement with (a) supports the ambiguity reading - tighten the two or three items and watch recurrence, symptom migration, and re-onset after schedule changes.
